newsitem.title: USA: Crow slams Wal-Mart for banning her record.
newsitem.headline: Crow slams Wal-Mart for banning her record.

text.p: Pop singer Sheryl Crow walked off with two Grammys on Wednesday and in triumph, took a swipe at the mighty Wal-Mart chain.

Crow, who won for best rock album and best female rock vocal, told reporters after the awards that she was surprised and hurt when Wal-Mart refused to sell her album "Sheryl Crow" last year because it contained a lyric criticizing the discount store chain.
"I was surprised and very pissed off," she said, adding that she came from a small town where Wal-Mart stores "wipes out mom and pop businesses."
Wal-Mart declined to sell the record because a song called "Love is a Good Thing" contained the lyric, "Watch our children kill each other with a gun they bought at the Wal-Mart discount chain."
"I think that is in direct opposition to the first amendment," she said.
The album sold over one million copies and remains in the top 40 several months after its release.
